notes: Identity verified independently from title page: Temporal Differences in Trait Self-Ascription: When the Self Is Seen as an Other; Emily Pronin and Lee Ross; Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 2006, 90(2), 197–209; DOI 10.1037/0022-3514.90.2.197. Supplied canonical text is a full primary journal article with Study 1 methods/results, subsequent studies and references. No PDF was supplied. Target matched by Study 1 undergraduate actor–observer comparison of present self versus friend, not by numeric matching or row order. The outcome is a single count of trait ascriptions rather than situational-variability responses. F(1, 61) = 7.42 and p = .008 belong to this same contrast. The omnibus F(3, 120) = 6.23 and self-present versus self-past F(1, 62) = 11.63 are different tests. Recruitment/sample total n = 123 spans four randomly assigned assessment groups; explicit group counts or critical-comparison analytic N are not supplied. No N inferred from degrees of freedom, and no arithmetic derivation performed. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
